title: John son of Zebedee
aliases: who is john son of zebedee
tell me about john son of zebedee
why is john son of zebedee important
summary: Matthew names John son of Zebedee among the fishermen Jesus calls, alongside his brother James and their father Zebedee. Luke later names John among the Twelve, and Acts includes him among the disciples gathered in Jerusalem. These references establish his call and group membership, but they do not by themselves identify him as the author of any New Testament book or describe his later ministry.
historical_context: Matthew 4:18–22 places John in a family fishing setting with James and their father Zebedee when Jesus calls them. Luke 6 and Acts 1 list John among the Twelve and the gathered disciples. The cited passages give this outline but do not provide a full chronology or later biography.
ancient_near_east_context: The call scene mentions a boat, fishing work, and a father and two sons. These details show the family work setting that John leaves in Matthew’s account; the passage does not provide enough information to generalize about all fishing households or their economic arrangements.
canonical_context: In these references John is identified as Zebedee’s son, James’s brother, and one of the Twelve. Other traditions associate the name John with New Testament writings, but these particular passages do not make that identification; they should be read for the identity and role they actually state.
literary_context: The references move from Matthew’s call scene to group lists in Luke and Acts. Matthew shows John leaving the boat and his father with James to follow Jesus; Luke 6 names him when the Twelve are appointed; Acts 1 places him among the disciples after Jesus’ departure. The texts give a clear place in the group while leaving John’s later actions largely outside these anchors.
covenantal_significance: The listed passages show John responding to Jesus’ call and belonging to the Twelve, the group around which the Gospel narrative gathers Jesus’ mission. They support that role in Matthew, Luke, and Acts, but do not establish a distinct later ministry or authorship claim for John.
canonical_role: John son of Zebedee serves as a canonical person anchor, connecting biographical context, key passages, and related places, events, and themes.

interpretive_notes.note: The apostolic role is about witness and commission, not private spiritual status.
The Gospels and Acts often show both calling and ongoing formation.
